column1: # TITLE: Expression profiling of lung cancer cell lines (UTSW Lung Panel V2)
# SUMMARY: Epithelial/mesenchymal transition (EMT) is associated with loss of cell adhesion molecules
column5: and proliferation in epithelial cancers. In non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC)
column6: EMT is associated with greater resistance to EGFR inhibitors. However
column7: its potential to predict response to other targeted drugs or chemotherapy has not been well characterized. The goal of this study was to develop a robust
column8: platform-independent EMT gene expression signature and to investigate the association of EMT and drug response in NSCLC. A 76-gene EMT signature was derived in 54 DNA-fingerprinted NSCLC cell lines and tested in an independent set of cell lines and in NSCLC patients from the BATTLE clinical trial. The signature classified cell lines as epithelial or mesenchymal independent of the microarray platform and correlated strongly with E-cadherin protein levels
column9: as measured by reverse phase protein array. Higher protein expression of Rab25 (in epithelial lines) and Axl (in mesenchymal lines)
column10: two signature genes associated with in EMT in other cancer types
column11: was also confirmed. Mesenchymal cell lines demonstrated significantly greater resistance to EGFR inhibition
column12: independent of EGFR mutation status and were more resistant to drugs targeting the PI3K/Akt pathway. We observed no association between EMT and response to cytotoxic chemotherapies
column15: and docetaxel monotherapy and/or doublets (p-values ?0.2). In NSCLC patients
column16: the EMT signature predicted 8-week disease control in the erlotinib arm
column17: but not in other treatment arms. In conclusion
column18: we have developed a robust EMT signature that predicts resistance to EGFR inhibitors and PI3K/Akt pathway inhibitors.
